title: Certificates of Deposit: Room Left Under the Term Total and the Tier's Largest Principal
content:
Two limits written into the tier terms of Piedmont Crescent Bank's Certificates of Deposit cap how much an in-term add-on can bring in. Each is expressed here as the room it leaves, measured on the certificate as it stands at the moment the add-on is made.

## Room under the term total

The room under the term total is the tier's total allowed for in-term add-ons in one term, less whatever sum was added earlier in the running term (nothing is deducted when there has been none). On a tier that allows no in-term add-on, this room is zero.

## Room under the tier's largest principal

The room under the tier's largest principal is the largest principal one certificate of the tier may hold, less the certificate's principal balance at the moment of the add-on. An add-on larger than this room would leave the certificate holding more than its tier permits.

## Worked example (hypothetical tier figures, chosen only to illustrate: term total USD 20000.00, largest principal USD 600000.00)

| Certificate as it stands | Add-on already made this term | Room under the term total | Room under the largest principal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Principal USD 95000.00 | none | 20000.00 less nothing, that is USD 20000.00 | 600000.00 less 95000.00, that is USD 505000.00 |
| Principal USD 590000.00 | none | USD 20000.00 | 600000.00 less 590000.00, that is USD 10000.00 |
| Principal USD 95000.00 | USD 7500.00 | 20000.00 less 7500.00, that is USD 12500.00 | USD 505000.00 |

## Point of judgement

**Does interest compounded since the add-on reduce the room under the term total?** No. Only add-on deposits of the current term are deducted from the term total; the room under the largest principal, by contrast, is measured from the whole principal balance, which includes compounded interest.
